name: Julian Assange
contribution: Founded WikiLeaks and built a globally influential model for publishing leaked primary documents.
whyIncluded: The contribution is structural: a publishing mechanism designed to move suppressed records into public view.
caveat: Inclusion concerns publishing architecture and public-record impact, not endorsement of every publication choice, political position or alleged act.

name: Chelsea Manning
contribution: Disclosed a large body of military and diplomatic records that drove global debate about war, secrecy and accountability.
whyIncluded: The record set became a major public evidence route into state conduct and the human consequences of conflict.
caveat: Inclusion recognises disclosure impact and personal risk; it does not resolve every legal or ethical argument about the release.

name: Laura Poitras
contribution: Documentary journalist whose work helped bring mass-surveillance evidence to a global audience and who supports press-freedom infrastructure.
whyIncluded: She translated complex primary evidence into durable public understanding while maintaining a strong source-protection focus.

sources.label: Freedom of the Press Foundation board

caveat: Inclusion recognises journalism and source-protection work, not endorsement of every editorial interpretation.

name: Frances Haugen
contribution: Released internal Facebook records and testified publicly about platform incentives, safety and governance.
whyIncluded: The disclosures created a documentary route into how a major platform assessed harms and trade-offs internally.
caveat: Inclusion recognises disclosure and testimony; it does not mean every interpretation of the documents is proven.

name: Thomas Drake
contribution: Former NSA official who raised concerns about surveillance, waste and constitutional risk.
whyIncluded: His case is a major route into the costs and legal hazards faced by national-security whistleblowers.
caveat: Inclusion recognises documented whistleblowing and public-interest debate, not every claim made by supporters or critics.

name: John Kiriakou
contribution: Former CIA officer who publicly confirmed aspects of the agency's post-9/11 torture program and later advocated for whistleblowers.
whyIncluded: His disclosures created a public route into secret detention, interrogation policy and accountability.
caveat: Inclusion recognises disclosure impact and personal consequences; it does not endorse every later statement.

name: William Binney
contribution: Former NSA technical director who became a prominent critic of mass-surveillance systems and intelligence oversight failures.
whyIncluded: His technical background made him an important public source on how surveillance systems can expand beyond targeted collection.
caveat: Some public claims remain disputed. Inclusion recognises documented service, dissent and public testimony, not acceptance of every technical or political conclusion.

name: Katharine Gun
contribution: Leaked a request connected to surveillance of UN delegations during the diplomatic build-up to the Iraq war.
whyIncluded: Her action created a direct documentary route into the pressure surrounding international war authorisation.
caveat: Inclusion recognises a documented disclosure and personal risk, not endorsement of every interpretation of the Iraq-war debate.

name: Glenn Greenwald
contribution: Journalist centrally involved in publishing the Snowden archive and known for adversarial reporting on state and media power.
whyIncluded: His work helped translate surveillance records into sustained public debate and legal scrutiny.
caveat: Inclusion recognises documented reporting impact; it does not endorse every opinion, alliance or later editorial judgment.

name: Seymour Hersh
contribution: Investigative journalist with a decades-long record of reporting on military, intelligence and government misconduct.
whyIncluded: His career demonstrates the role of protected sources and persistent investigation in challenging official narratives.
caveat: Individual reports vary in verification and dispute. Inclusion recognises career impact, not automatic acceptance of every story.

name: Matt Taibbi
contribution: Journalist covering financial power, media incentives, censorship disputes and internal platform records.
whyIncluded: His work supplies a public route into institutional media behaviour and content-moderation controversies.
caveat: Inclusion recognises reporting and public reach; it does not endorse every framing, source choice or political conclusion.

name: Michael Shellenberger
lane: Independent reporting on censorship and institutions
contribution: Founder of Public and a prominent writer on censorship, institutional failure and government-platform relationships.
whyIncluded: His outlet explicitly emphasises subscriber funding, source protection and reporting on powerful institutions.
caveat: Inclusion recognises documented reporting and public debate; it does not endorse every claim or policy position.

name: Sarah Harrison
contribution: WikiLeaks journalist and editor known for supporting high-risk sources and publication work.
whyIncluded: Source protection and logistical support are essential parts of transparency infrastructure but are often less visible than publication itself.
caveat: Inclusion recognises public source-support and publishing work; it does not settle every legal or ethical dispute involving WikiLeaks.
